common.tagline: Practice game development on your laptop. Build your final game together in Godot.
common.brandLine: Practice Godot concepts in the browser

landing.promise: Practice game development on your laptop. Build your final game together in Godot.
landing.body: Godot Learning Lab helps high school students learn Godot 4 concepts through short explanations and lightweight browser practice, then build a 2D game in teams in the real Godot editor.
landing.point1: Eight modules: scenes, movement, collision, input, signals, state, timers, and a complete game.
landing.point2: Practice runs on modest laptops without installing Godot.
landing.point3: Teachers give feedback and form project teams.
landing.honest: The practice here simulates Godot concepts; it is not Godot. Final games are built in the real Godot editor on school computers.
landing.cta: Sign in with your school account

privacy.title: Privacy notice
privacy.draftNotice: This notice is a draft that the school must review and approve before use with real student data. It makes no legal compliance claim.

collect.p: Your school-approved display name, school email (only in the sign-in system), practice results, survey answers, team project proposals and notes, personal contribution statements, and teacher feedback and scores.

why.p: To teach, give feedback, plan school-computer access, form teams, and assess projects. Not for advertising or tracking.

who.p: Your teacher sees their class's work and survey answers. Teammates see the team proposal and milestones. Classmates cannot see your survey answers, personal contributions, or individual scores.

notCollected.h: What we do not ask for
notCollected.p: Home address, date of birth, social media accounts, medical information, or family income. No ads, public profiles, student-to-student messaging, or third-party analytics.

surveys.p: Surveys are linked to your name so your teacher can help. Sensitive questions are optional and offer "Prefer not to answer".

keep.p: Proposed: until the end of term plus 90 days, then deleted under the school's procedure. Backups and exported files follow provider limits and school rules.

rights.p: You or your parent/guardian can ask for a copy or deletion of data through the school contact below.

storage.p: Data is stored in the database service chosen by the school. Final game files are stored in school storage, not in this app.

plan.title: 12-week plan & rubric
plan.subtitle: A configurable template; printable.
plan.weeksHelp: Set due dates on the Assignments page. Extra modules, absences, and school events may stretch this to 14–16 weeks; do not cut individual editor practice.
plan.capacity: Access check: supervised machine-hours = machines × reserved hours. Demand = teams × team editor hours + individual practice. If demand exceeds supply, extend the calendar or simplify scope.
plan.rubricHelp: 60 team artifact points, 40 individual learning/contribution points. Survey opinions and device ownership earn or lose nothing. Share the rubric before proposals.
plan.anchors: Anchors: excellent = 100% of weight; meets = 75%; developing = 50%; beginning = 25%; no evidence = 0%. Intermediate scores are allowed with a short note.
plan.individualEvidence: Individual evidence: record editor-task observations (create/instance a scene, input action, signal, or debugging) at each milestone, and check role rotation in contribution statements. Browser practice results are formative, not exam evidence.
